season_context.local_season_notes: Trade press notes an extended hot autumn that delays seasonal buying, so retailers lean on suede, leather and colour to signal autumn. Nov-Apr spans Shichi-Go-San in November, New Year sales, Coming-of-Age ceremonies in January and March graduations, followed by the April new-school and new-job season.

sources.title: WWDJAPAN 2026-27 AW women's real trend issue (PR Times)
Fashion Week de Tokyo PE27 (FashionUnited FR)
Rakuten Fashion Week TOKYO 27SS show schedule

trends.name: Earth tones sharpened with burgundy and black
trends.summary: Tokyo street crowds in early September favoured browns, khaki and olive, made sharper with deep burgundy accents and black pieces such as faux-leather barrel trousers; observers noted the palette reads more autumnal than summery.

trends.name: Harajuku-style print clashing
trends.summary: Maximalist dressing mixes clashing prints and colours: collage-printed mesh with tulle, playing-card and baroque prints, camo denim and sheer leopard skirts layered together for a personal, rule-breaking look.

trends.name: Denim as the wardrobe base
trends.summary: Denim appeared everywhere in Tokyo street style, from heavy structured jeans and shirts to jackets, culottes and tonal layering, sometimes with Western touches like cowboy hats and embroidered boots.

trends.name: Oversized, deliberately unbalanced layering
trends.summary: Street style around the SS27 shows centred on oversized cuts, dropped shoulders and intentionally off-kilter layering, with men leaning on minimal monochrome tailoring and low-key technical outerwear plus wide-leg trousers and culottes.

trends.name: Fringe as accent or statement
trends.summary: Fringing showed up on boots, corsets, dresses and skirts, from long macrame fringe on a denim trucker jacket to laser-cut fringe dresses and yellow leather fringe boots.

trends.name: Kimono and hakama references in daywear
trends.summary: Attendees reworked Japanese dress codes into street outfits: kimono-like wraps cinched with obi-style belts, hakama-cut skirt-trousers in jacquard and deconstructed oversized shapes in the avant-garde Tokyo tradition.

trends.name: Kimono-derived cutting at Yohji Yamamoto
trends.summary: The label's AW26 womenswear builds its pattern-cutting around the kimono, reinterpreting the traditional garment in several ways across the line now in its stores.

trends.name: Classic tailoring loosened with accent colour
trends.summary: WWDJAPAN's real-trend issue frames AW26-27 womenswear around classic, elegant tailored jackets that brands personalise, with a pop of accent colour as the key styling move alongside browns and greys.

trends.name: Suede and leather to signal autumn in a long summer
trends.summary: Because hot weather now stretches into autumn, Japanese retailers use suede and leather pieces to create an autumn mood early, a tactic highlighted by select-shop directors coping with cautious spending.

trends.name: Cream, cocoa, teal and vivid purple palette
trends.summary: A Japanese fabric-sourcing platform names warm cream white and chocolate brown as neutrals, deep blue-green teal and bright purple as rich tones, and a yellow-green as the accent for AW26-27 outerwear fabrics.

trends.name: Lustre and napped textures with PFAS-free finishes
trends.summary: Fabric picks for AW26-27 stress sheen and touch: rayon-cotton satin, triacetate velour, organza, napped double-weave suede and corduroy, plus recycled nylon, plant-based faux leather and fluorine-free water repellents.

trends.name: Sculptural, curved silhouettes
trends.summary: Tokyo's AW26 runways pushed garments into sculpture: Enfold's curved asymmetric cuts, Ryunosuke Okazaki's wire and stretch constructions and a dramatically flared-shoulder long dress at Grounds.

trends.name: Photographic prints of everyday scenes
trends.summary: Kotohayokozawa, Yoshiokubo and Agnes B printed photographs of ordinary objects and places onto clothes, either as one large image or tiled into collages.

trends.name: Diamond-quilted outerwear
trends.summary: Diamond quilting ran through AW26 Tokyo collections from Pays des Fees, Viviano and Eitaro, used mostly on knee-length coats and other cold-weather layers.

trends.name: 18th and 19th century references
trends.summary: Houga, Agnes B and Mukcyen drew on period dress for AW26, using high necklines, layered construction and subdued colour.

trends.name: Creepy-cute kawaii
trends.summary: Designers blended tulle and ruffles with streetwear, early-2000s nostalgia, patchwork and childlike motifs, giving the kawaii aesthetic a slightly eerie edge; Taiwanese labels and Yusho Kobayashi led the look in Tokyo.

trends.name: Utility outerwear with tartan, fur and distressing
trends.summary: Tokyo FW26 street style layered heavy zip denim jackets and technical coats over tartan and fur-trimmed pieces, with frayed hems, aged fabrics and asymmetric deconstruction mixing designer and outdoor gear.

trends.name: Quiet, fabric-led Japanese menswear
trends.summary: Labels such as Auralee, Comoli, A.Presse, Kaptain Sunshine, Nanamica and Goldwin are championed for relaxed, worn-in fits, softened workwear, archival references and technical outerwear made for daily city wear rather than logos.

trends.name: Fit-first, value-driven luxury buying
trends.summary: Japan's luxury market is projected to grow slightly in 2026, with tourists about a third of sales; young Japanese shoppers rank fit, design and durability far above brand name and still prefer buying in stores.

trends.name: Underwater and mermaid motifs
trends.summary: SS27 Tokyo shows dived under the sea: scale-like sequin dresses and knitted octopus bags at Yushokobayashi, coral skirts with dolphin and jellyfish prints at Charinyeh, and Breton tops with sailor hats at Meg Miura Wardrobe.

trends.name: Athletic nomad
trends.summary: Yoshiokubo mixed Mongolian references with running kit for SS27: short running shorts, running vests and light jackets finished with flowers and cord details borrowed from quick-release fasteners.

trends.name: Sheer, flowing layers
trends.summary: Charinyeh, Anna Choi and Eitaro used transparent, fluid fabrics in wide flared or enveloping shapes, building outfits through layering and gradient colour for SS27.

trends.name: Black power suits with 1970s collars
trends.summary: Perry Jones, Keisukeyoshida and Fetico showed all-black suits with flared shoulders, long pointed seventies-style shirt collars or contrast lapels, boxy or waisted jackets and wider trousers, styled with heels.

trends.name: Multiplied and displaced collars
trends.summary: RequaL stretched several collars over the shoulders with stacked ties, Mitsuru Okazaki ringed collars as a central motif and Seivson rebuilt a pleated piece into an asymmetric corseted coat-dress.

trends.name: Wax-resist dyeing and lacquer craft
trends.summary: C JEAN's Tokyo debut for SS27 used roketsu wax-resist dyeing from a Kyoto workshop and lacquered bags made with a Taiwanese lacquer artist, foregrounding artisanal surface techniques.

trends.name: Marine embroidery and sequin embellishment
trends.summary: Charinyeh embroidered octopus motifs onto coral-like skirts while Yushokobayashi covered dresses in glossy scale-like sequins and layered rough netting with lace for SS27.
